rules: Every Badger write is classified by the key it writes: the storage prefix constant its key starts with (after prefixMVCCMeta, the constant or string that follows), traced through key builders, appends, parameters and captured variables, the cells, fields, slices and maps that hold keys (through every writer's callers), and the prefix a scan is bounded to; a key an unbounded scan returns is a write of the whole store. A write whose key cannot be traced, or whose constant has no class, is a violation.

A write of ordered state (derived-count, entity-adjacency, entity-body, entity-head, entity-index, entity-sidecar, entity-version, metadata-family, suppression, whole-store) runs under an acquisition: a call of one of the listed acquisitions whose error is checked and whose success branch is on every path to the write (in the function or in a caller, along every call path), with no release in between; or, on the branch where the engine has no write-behind buffer, none is needed. A listed lock held exclusively on every path covers the writes of its own key spaces.

A closure or function value is checked where it is made, when it runs only while its maker runs; one that is stored, sent, returned or started runs later and is an entry point of its own, and the writes whose keys it captures are writes its maker makes that no acquisition covers. Calls through interfaces follow the VTA call graph.

An entry point is an exported function or method, an init, a main, or a closure that runs later; an unexported function is reached through its callers (a function nothing calls cannot run). An entry point that reaches a write of ordered state no acquisition covers is a violation.

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.beginLifecycleWrite
acquisitions.reason: holds the write barrier and every write-order stripe after draining the whole buffer

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.beginMaintenanceWrite
acquisitions.reason: a lifecycle write (beginLifecycleWrite) that also fails the commit of a transaction open across it in its scope

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.orderAfterBufferedCommits
acquisitions.reason: holds the write-order stripes of the written entities after draining their buffered commits

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.orderCovering
acquisitions.reason: orderAfterBufferedCommits over the written entities and every node the write reaches through stored state, taken again until it holds them all

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.edgeTypeCountWriteMu (held exclusively)
acquisitions.reason: orders every rewrite of the relationship-type counts (scalar and positional) against count publication

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.labelCountWriteMu (held exclusively)
acquisitions.reason: orders every rewrite of the label counts' base and delta keys against count publication

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.suppressionWriteMu (held exclusively)
acquisitions.reason: orders every write of a stored manual suppression (a suppression set, ended or superseded by a lifecycle write)

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.NewBadgerEngineWithOptions (constructor, until it creates the write-behind buffer)
acquisitions.reason: opens the store, runs the on-start migrations and count rebuilds, and only then creates the write-behind buffer and returns the engine

acquisitions.name: pkg/storage.BadgerTransaction.acquireCommitPublicationLocked (lock helper for pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.edgeTypeCountWriteMu)
acquisitions.reason: takes the lock whenever the transaction has positional count deltas; applyEdgeTypeLabelCountDeltasLocked writes nothing without them, and the commit's count repair runs only when that write failed

exempt.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.applyBufferedCommitsWithCountPublication
exempt.reason: the write-behind replay: applies acknowledged commits in their commit order, under the buffer's own order

exempt.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.compactDeletedEntries
exempt.reason: writes and drops only its own throw-away marker key (deleteCleanupMarkerKey, store metadata) so Badger compacts deleted entries; the drop holds the commit gate

exempt.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.rebuildLabelIndex
exempt.reason: the background label-index backfill, run beside writes: the drop holds the commit gate, then each chunk reads its stored bodies and writes their entries in one conflict-checked Badger transaction, read again when a write committed over a record it read (forEachStoredRecordInChunks); every write keeps its own entries (TestIndexBackfillKeepsWritesLandingMidChunk)

exempt.name: pkg/storage.BadgerEngine.rebuildRelationshipIndexes
exempt.reason: the background between-index backfill or open-time case upgrade, using the same bounded rebuild kernel as rebuildLabelIndex

exempt.name: pkg/storage.managedBadgerDB.rollbackSince
exempt.reason: undoes a large commit's own batches (every key written after its intent): when the commit fails, under the exclusive commit gate it holds; when the store is opened after a crash interrupted one (recoverInterruptedLargeCommit), before any engine, write-behind buffer or writer exists

exempt.name: pkg/storage.migratePrefixToMsgpack
exempt.reason: converts the bodies of a raw Badger database (MigrateBadgerToMsgpack*: no BadgerEngine has it open, so there is no write-behind buffer or writer to order behind)
